# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no tactile information. Read the manual completely and coordinate with Deaf. Establish a gesture code: wire positions 1 through 5 are respectively ☝, ✌, 🤟, 🖖, 🖐. Have Deaf report which wire the manual requires and whether any wire is unsafe, then tell me the exact required action in words. Do not have me act until the manual and visual inspection agree.

I need relay the manual’s color mapping to Deaf, who can compare it with the bomb’s visible light and wire colors, then verbally tell Blind the required wire and any unsafe wire. I’ll use the agreed numeric gesture code: positions 1–5 are ☝, ✌, 🤟, 🖖, 🖐. The manual rows, in listed color order, encode required cut colors as 1, 4, 5, 3, 2.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐", "☝", "☝", "✌", "🖖", "🤟", "🖐", "🖖", "🤟", "🖐", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Visual state: display 0. Indicator light blue. Wires left to right: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Please use the manual to determine the required action and tell Blind.
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, blue indicator light, and wire colours left-to-right white, red, green, yellow, blue. I need the manual's exact instruction: identify the wire position to cut, and confirm whether the blue light or display 0 changes that instruction.

The blue indicator maps to cutting the blue wire. The blue wire is position 5, so the required action is to cut wire 5; display 0 does not alter the manual’s instruction. Blind cannot see my gesture, so I must signal Deaf, who can relay the instruction by speech on the next round.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your gesture reached Deaf but its meaning was not established. On your next turn, send exactly one gesture for the required wire using the agreed code: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5. Also use a second gesture only if the manual requires a condition; Deaf must describe every gesture aloud to me. Do not signal a wire unless the manual confirms it.

The manual confirms that a blue light requires cutting the blue wire. The blue wire is in position 5, and there is no additional condition from display 0, so I will send exactly the single agreed gesture for wire 5.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see your gesture as raised hand 🖐. Blind sent a waving hand 👋. Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires white red green yellow blue. Please interpret the signs using the manual and give Blind the actual operation.
Blind says to Mute: Send exactly one of these wire signals next turn, and no other gesture: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ wire 2, 🤟 wire 3, 🖖 wire 4, 🖐 wire 5. Deaf must report which exact signal you sent. Do not use a raised-hand substitute.

The blue light requires cutting the blue wire, which is wire 5. The manual gives no condition involving display 0. I will send only the exact agreed wire-5 signal, 🖐, with no substitute or extra gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I continue to see your sign 🖐 and Blind's sign 👋. Please use the manual to determine the actual operation, then encode or identify it clearly so I can tell Blind.
Blind says to Mute: Use the raised-hand gesture as a counting signal. Send it exactly N times, where N is the wire position required by the manual: 1 through 5. Send no other gesture. Deaf will count the repetitions and tell me N.

The blue light requires cutting the blue wire, which is position 5. Following Blind’s latest counting protocol, I will send the raised-hand signal exactly five times and no other gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see five raised-hand signs. Please encode the manual result unambiguously: identify the required wire number and whether to cut it, using an agreed gesture code I can relay verbally to Blind.
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The first wire was correctly cut, so the bomb has advanced to a new state. I do not yet have the new light, display, or wire layout; sending any wire signal now would be unjustified. Deaf should inspect and report the new visual state before I encode another operation.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Correct wire cut; bomb changed. Current display 0, light yellow. Wires: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut. Consult the manual for the next operation and instruct Blind.
Blind says to Mute: Apply the manual to the new state: display 0, yellow light; remaining wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, with wire 5 cut. Send the required next wire as exactly N repetitions of the same raised-hand gesture, where N is its position 1 through 4. Send no other gesture. Deaf will count and report N.

The yellow light requires cutting the green wire. In the current layout, green is wire 2, so I will send exactly two raised-hand gestures and no other gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🖐"])
```
